newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian steel mill rejects shareholder claims.
newsitem.headline: Russian steel mill rejects shareholder claims.

text.p: Russia's largest steel mill, Novolipetsk Metals Combine, rebuffed a foreign shareholder's attempt for board representation on Friday with a rare public statement in what is seen as a shareholders' rights litmus test.

Renaissance Capital, whose Sputnik Fund investment arm owns nine percent of Novolipetsk shares, said on Tuesday it had filed a complaint with the local prosecutor after the mill failed to include elections to the board in its annual meeting agenda.

But AOOT Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat (Novolipetsk or NLMK) said in a statement Russian law did not require including the elections on the agenda, which continuing legal proceedings had made undesirable.

"Given unfinished litigation...to include the question of electing a new board of directors on the agenda of the annual general meeting would lead to yet another round of conflict between the company and individual shareholders," it said.

In three separate rulings, a regional court last month ordered the plant to include nominees from Sputnik and fellow shareholders Bank MFK (ICFI) and Monaco-based Cambridge Capital Management on a list of candidates to a new board of directors.
The Novolipetsk statement said the court orders had not yet come into effect.
Renaissance Capital said its position was unchanged.
"There's clearly no legal ground for NLMK's position," a spokesman said. "The statement follows their legal arguments that they put forward in three court cases that they've lost."
Cambridge Captital Management owns 17.2 percent of shares in the mill and Bank MFK owns about 15 percent.
